title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — Minaya brings the daughters home; Muño Gustioz asks the king for justice (tiradas 132–133, lines 2863–2967)
part: Tiradas 132–133 · Minaya brings the daughters home; Muño Gustioz asks the king for justice (lines 2863–2967)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 306–311, lines 2863–2967 (tiradas 132–133). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t:
Lloravan de los ojos las dueñas e Álbar Fáñez,
e Per Vermu[doz] otro tanto las ha;
sentences.l:
Were-weeping from the eyes the ladies and Álbar Fáñez,
and Per Vermu[doz] as-much to-them has (said);
sentences.i: The ladies wept, and Álvar Fáñez with them, and Per Vermudoz spoke to them in the same way:
sentences.n: Tirada 132 (assonance á, á-e) — Minaya and his cousins leave San Esteban; the Çid rides out to receive them (Pidal: Minaya y sus primas parten de San Esteban.—El Cid sale a recibirlos). The line-ends run Fáñez, ha, ayades, mal, ganar, vengar, fazen, cavalgar …, with menssaje, sale, faze, padre, madre: stressed á, sometimes with an e after it; a new assonance, a new tirada. Lloravan de los ojos, 'they wept from their eyes', the epic way of saying it (as in v. 1). The second line is hard. Pidal's note to v. 2864: 'Verso dificil. Lidforss corrige: otro tanto conortado las ha. Pudiera ser: otro tanto fablado las ha, "así las habló"' — 'A difficult line. Lidforss corrects: otro tanto conortado las ha ["has comforted them as much"]. It might be: otro tanto fablado las ha, "thus he spoke to them"' (dificil so printed, without the accent; his own quotes are single, ours double inside his). As printed, otro tanto las ha, 'as much he has (done/said) to them', with las 'them' for the ladies; the speech that follows is Per Vermudoz's, as Pidal's note to v. 2867 says. The rendering follows Pidal's second guess, and is not certain. Vermu[doz], the doz Pidal's. Álbar printed with an accent here.

sentences.t:
“Don Elvira e doña Sol, cuydado non ayades,
quando vos sodes sanas e bivas e sin otro mal.
Buen casamiento perdiestes, mejor podredes ganar.
Aun veamos el día que vos podamos vengar!”
sentences.l:
“Don Elvira and doña Sol, care not may-you-have,
since you are sound and alive and without other harm.
Good marriage you-lost, better you-will-be-able to-win.
Yet may-we-see the day that you we-may-be-able to-avenge!”
sentences.i: “Doña Elvira and Doña Sol, take no care for it, since you are whole and alive and have come to no other harm. A good marriage you have lost; a better you may yet win. May we live to see the day when we can avenge you!”
sentences.n: cuydado non ayades, 'may you have no care': ayades, present subjunctive of aver, with non as a prohibition. quando, 'since, seeing that'. sodes = sois; bivas = vivas. perdiestes = perdisteis; podredes = podréis, the old -edes ending. Aun veamos … podamos, present subjunctives of wish, 'may we yet see … that we may be able'. Pidal's note to v. 2867: 'El solo hecho del abandono y malos tratos basta para dar como disuelto el matrimonio, sino que se espere decisión ninguna eclesiástica ni civil. Lo mismo que aquí Pedro Vermúdez, se expresa luego el Cid, 2893, 3156-57, 3206, y el segundo casamiento de Elvira y Sol se hace sin la menor dificultad' — 'The mere fact of the abandonment and ill-treatment is enough to hold the marriage dissolved, without any decision, church or civil, being awaited [sino que is as printed]. As Pedro Vermúdez does here, the Cid expresses himself later, 2893, 3156-57, 3206, and the second marriage of Elvira and Sol is made without the least difficulty.' Don Elvira, as printed (house: 'Doña Elvira').

sentences.t: Í yazen essa noche, e tan grand gozo que fazen.
sentences.l: There they-lie that night, and so great joy that they-make.
sentences.i: There they lodge that night, and great is the joy they make.
sentences.n: Í = y, 'there' (allí), printed with a capital and an accent; not 'and'. yazen, 'they lie', i.e. lodge, rest (yazer, as yazredes at v. 2635). tan grand gozo que fazen, 'such great joy they make', an exclamation set loosely beside the first half; fazen = hacen, f- for h-, giving á-e.

sentences.t: Otro dia mañana pienssan de cavalgar.
sentences.l: Other day morning they-think of to-ride.
sentences.i: Early the next morning they make ready to ride.
sentences.n: Otro dia mañana, 'the next day in the morning' (dia unaccented, as printed). pienssan de cavalgar, penssar de + infinitive, 'to set about', the stock formula.

sentences.t:
Los de Sant Estevan escurriéndolos van
fata Rio d' amor, dándoles solaz;
d' allent se espidieron dellos, piénssanse de tornar.
e Minaya con las dueñas iva cabadelant.
sentences.l:
Those of Sant Estevan escorting-them go
as-far-as Rio d' amor, giving-them solace;
from-beyond themselves took-leave of-them, they-think-themselves to return.
and Minaya with the ladies was-going onward.
sentences.i: The men of San Esteban ride with them as an escort as far as Río d'Amor, keeping them company and cheer; there, on the far side, they took their leave of them and set out to go home, and Minaya went on ahead with the ladies.
sentences.n: Los de Sant Estevan, 'those of San Esteban', its townsmen (tirada 131). escurriéndolos van, ir + gerund, 'go escorting them' (escurrir of an escort on the road, as at vv. 2640, 2652). fata = hasta, 'as far as'. Pidal's note to v. 2872: 'Rio d'amor, hoy desconocido, debía estar al Este de San Esteban de Gormaz' — 'Río d'Amor, unknown today, must have lain east of San Esteban de Gormaz'. dándoles solaz, 'giving them solace', pleasant company on the way. d' allent = de allende, 'from beyond': here 'from there, on the far side'; just where is not said. se espidieron = se despidieron, 'took their leave'. piénssanse de tornar, 'they set about returning'. Pidal ends tornar with a full stop and begins the next line with a small e, as printed. iva cabadelant, 'went onward' (cab adelant, as at v. 858).

sentences.t:
Troçieron Alcoçeva, adiestro de[x]an Gormaz,
o dizen Bado de Rey, allá ivan p[as]sar,
a la casa de Berlanga posada presa han.
sentences.l:
They-crossed Alcoçeva, on-the-right they-leave Gormaz,
where they-call Bado de Rey, there they-went to-cross,
at the town of Berlanga lodging taken they-have.
sentences.i: They crossed the Alcoceba, leaving Gormaz on their right; at the place they call Bado de Rey, there they went over the river; and in the town of Berlanga they have taken their lodging.
sentences.n: Troçieron, 'they crossed, passed' (troçir, as at v. 2653). Pidal's note to v. 2875: 'Alcoceva, hoy "barranco de Alcoceba", el cual desagua en la misma punta del gran recodo que el Duero forma alrededor del castillo de Gormaz' — 'Alcoceva, today the "ravine of Alcoceba", which drains out at the very point of the great bend the Duero makes around the castle of Gormaz'. adiestro, 'on the right hand'. de[x]an = dejan, the x Pidal's. o = ó, 'where' (as at v. 2618). Pidal's note to v. 2876: 'Bado de Rey, hoy "Vadorrey", despoblado a la izquierda del Duero, en el camino de Berlanga a Gormaz' — 'today "Vadorrey", an abandoned settlement on the left of the Duero, on the road from Berlanga to Gormaz'; the name means 'the King's Ford' (bado = vado). ivan p[as]sar, 'they went to cross', ir + bare infinitive: the letters in Pidal's italic are given as established, but how far his italic runs in this word is not certain on the scan. Pidal's note to v. 2877: 'casa, "población, lugar"' — 'town, place'; he goes on: 'Berlanga, pueblo y castillo a la izquierda del Duero, distante de Gormaz 13 kilómetros, y de San Esteban, 30' — 'a town and castle on the left of the Duero, 13 kilometres from Gormaz and 30 from San Esteban'. posada presa han, 'they have taken lodging', the participle presa (of prender) agreeing with posada.

sentences.i: Early the next morning they take to the road again and went to lodge at the place they call Medinaceli; and from Medinaceli to Molina they go in one more day.
sentences.n: métense a andar, 'they set themselves to travel'. Pidal's note to v. 2879: 'a qual dizen Medina, "a la que llaman Medinaceli' — 'to the one they call Medinaceli' (his closing quote is not printed); Medina is Medinaceli in the English, as in earlier parts. ivan albergar, 'they went to lodge', ir + bare infinitive again. The same note to v. 2877 goes on with the stages: 'La segunda jornada de Berlanga a Medinaceli es de 46 kilómetros, y la tercera, de Medina a Molina (2880), es de 58 kilómetros. Esta demasiado larga jornada era corriente (1476-1534, 1542, 2657), y estaba impuesta por la importancia de los dos puntos extremos' — 'The second day's ride, from Berlanga to Medinaceli, is 46 kilometres, and the third, from Medina to Molina (2880), 58 kilometres. This over-long day's ride was usual (1476-1534, 1542, 2657), and was imposed by the importance of the two places at either end.' en otro día, 'in another day', one more stage.

sentences.t:
al moro Avengalvón de coraçón le plaz,
saliólos a reçebir de buena voluntad,
por amor de mio Çid rica cena les da.
sentences.l:
to-the Moor Avengalvón from heart it-pleases-him,
he-went-out-them to receive of good will,
for love of my Çid rich supper to-them he-gives.
sentences.i: The Moor Avengalvón is glad of it with all his heart; he rode out to receive them with right good will, and for love of my Çid he gives them a rich supper.
sentences.n: al moro Avengalvón … le plaz: the person named with a and taken up again by le, 'to the Moor … it pleases him'. plaz = place, cut short, giving á. de coraçón, 'from the heart'. saliólos a reçebir = salió a recibirlos, the pronoun drawn up onto the first verb. de buena voluntad, 'with good will'. por amor de mio Çid, 'for love of my Çid', Avengalvón's friendship with the Çid (vv. 1464, 2636).

sentences.t: Dent pora Valençia adeliñechos van.
sentences.l: From-there towards Valençia straight they-go.
sentences.i: From there they make straight for Valencia.
sentences.n: Dent = dende, 'from there'. pora = para. Pidal's note to v. 2884: 'adeliñeche, participio irregular, sinónimo de adeliñado, 1984, "en derechura"' — 'an irregular participle, the same as adeliñado, 1984, "straight on"'; the text has the plural adeliñechos, agreeing with the travellers.

sentences.i: The message came to him who was born in a good hour: at once he mounts and rides out to receive them, playing at arms as he went, and great is the joy he makes.
sentences.n: Al que en buen ora nasco, 'to him who was born in a good hour', the formula (nasco = nació). menssaje, 'message', giving á-e. privado, 'quickly' (an adverb). Pidal's note to v. 2887: '"jugaba las armas", v. 1577' — 'he was playing at arms': armas iva teniendo, the display of horsemanship and mock combat made on receiving someone (as v. 2896, and at a departure, vv. 2613, 2673). grant gozo que faze, the exclamation of v. 2869 again.

sentences.t:
Mio Çid a sus fijas ívalas abraçar,
besándolas a amas, tornós de sonrrisar:
sentences.l:
My Çid his daughters went-them to-embrace,
kissing-them both, turned-himself to smiling:
sentences.i: My Çid went to embrace his daughters, and, kissing them both, broke into a smile:
sentences.n: a sus fijas ívalas abraçar: the daughters named first, then taken up by las; ívalas = las iva, the pronoun of abraçar drawn up onto iva: 'he went to embrace them', ir + bare infinitive. besándolas a amas, 'kissing them both' (amas = ambas). tornós de sonrrisar = se tornó de sonreír, 'he turned to smiling', i.e. began to smile; tornós, the se cut to s.

sentences.t:
“¿Venides, mis fijas? Dios vos curie de mal!
Yo tomé el casamiento, mas non osé dezir al.
sentences.l:
“Come-you, my daughters? God you may-guard from harm!
I took the marriage, but not I-dared to-say other.
sentences.i: “You are come, my daughters! God keep you from harm! I accepted the marriage, but I did not dare to say otherwise.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 2890: '¿Venides? (comp. 204) y Dios vos curie (compárese 1396), fórmulas habituales de saludo' — '"Are you come?" (compare 204) and "God keep you" (compare 1396), the usual formulas of greeting'. Venides = venís. curie, present subjunctive of curiar, 'guard, keep'. tomé el casamiento, 'I accepted the marriage', the match the king proposed (tiradas 102–104). al, 'other thing, otherwise' (as sines al, v. 2255): he could not refuse his lord.

sentences.t:
Plega al Criador, que en çielo está,
que vos vea mejor casadas d' aquí en adelant.
De mios yernos de Carrión Dios me faga vengar!”
sentences.l:
May-it-please to-the Creator, who in heaven is,
that you I-may-see better married from here onward.
Of my sons-in-law of Carrión God me may-make to-avenge!”
sentences.i: May it please the Creator, who is in heaven, that from now on I may see you better married. God grant me vengeance on my sons-in-law of Carrión!”
sentences.n: Plega, present subjunctive of plazer, 'may it please'. vea, 'I may see'. d' aquí en adelant, 'from here on'. This is the line Pidal's note to v. 2867 cites: the Çid speaks of a better marriage as if the first were already undone. yernos, 'sons-in-law'. Dios me faga vengar, 'may God make me avenge (myself)', i.e. grant me vengeance. The speech ends here.

sentences.i: The daughters kissed their father's hands. Playing at arms they rode into the city, and Doña Ximena their mother made great joy over them.
sentences.n: Besaron las manos … al padre, 'kissed the hands to the father', the dative for whose hands; padre and madre give á-e. Teniendo ivan armas, 'they went playing at arms', the display of v. 2887 again. entráronse = se entraron, 'they went in'. cibdad = ciudad. fizo = hizo.

sentences.t:
El que en buen ora nasco non quiso tardar,
fablós con los sos en su poridad,
al rey Alfons de Castiella penssó de enbiar.
sentences.l:
He who in good hour was-born not wanted to-delay,
spoke-himself with the his in his privacy,
to-the king Alfons of Castiella he-thought of to-send.
sentences.i: He who was born in a good hour would make no delay: he spoke with his men in secret counsel, and set about sending to King Alfonso of Castile.
sentences.n: El que en buen ora nasco, the formula once more. fablós = se fabló, 'he spoke'. los sos, 'his (men)', sos = sus. en su poridad, 'in his secret council' (poridad, 'privacy, secret conference', as at vv. 1880, 1941). penssó de enbiar, 'he set about sending' (penssar de + infinitive). The tirada ends on the sending; the message itself opens the next tirada, with a new assonance.

sentences.t:
“¿O eres, Muño Gustioz, mio vassallo de pro.
en buen ora te crié a tí en la mi cort!
sentences.l:
“Where are-you, Muño Gustioz, my vassal of worth.
in good hour you I-reared you in the my court!
sentences.i: “Where are you, Muño Gustioz, my worthy vassal? In a good hour I brought you up in my court!
sentences.n: Tirada 133 (assonance ó, ó-e) — the Çid sends Muño Gustioz to ask the king for justice; Muño finds the king at Sahagún and sets out his message; the king promises redress (Pidal: El Cid envía a Muño Gustioz que pida al rey justicia.—Muño halla al rey en Sahagún, y le expone su mensaje.—El rey promete reparación). The line-ends run pro, cort, Alfons, coraçón, Carrión …, with cortes, noches, Corpes, ifançones: stressed ó, sometimes with an e after it. ¿O eres …: O = ó, 'where' (as at v. 2618), the Çid calling for his man; Pidal closes the question with a full stop and begins the next line with a small e, as printed. de pro, 'of worth'. te crié a tí, 'I reared you', the pronoun said twice (te … a tí); criar, 'to bring up' in one's household: Muño Gustioz is one of the Çid's own criados, the bond the Çid calls on now. la mi cort, article + possessive.

sentences.t:
Lieves el mandado a Castiella al rey Alfons;
por mí bésale la mano d' alma e de coraçón,
sentences.l:
May-you-carry the message to Castiella to-the king Alfons;
for me kiss-to-him the hand from soul and from heart,
sentences.i: Carry this message to Castile, to King Alfonso: kiss his hand for me, with all my soul and heart,
sentences.n: Lieves, present subjunctive of levar (llevar) used as a command, 'carry'. el mandado, 'the message'. bésale, imperative + le, 'kiss his …'. d' alma e de coraçón, 'with soul and heart', the pair said again at v. 2907.

sentences.t:
—qu[o]mo yo so s[o] vassallo, e el[le] es mio señor,—
desta desondra que me an fecha ifantes de Carrión
quel pese al buen rey d' alma e de coraçón.
sentences.l:
—as I am his vassal, and he is my lord,—
of-this dishonour that to-me have done Infantes of Carrión
that-to-him it-may-grieve to-the good king from soul and from heart.
sentences.i: — as I am his vassal and he is my lord — and beg that this dishonour the Infantes of Carrión have done me may grieve the good king to the depths of his soul and heart.
sentences.n: qu[o]mo = como, the o Pidal's. so = soy; s[o] = su, the o Pidal's. el[le] = él, the le Pidal's. an fecha, 'have done', the participle agreeing with desondra. quel = que le. Pidal's note to v. 2907: 'bésale la mano quel pese, "ruégale que le pese", v. 179' — 'kiss his hand that it may grieve him, "beg him that it may grieve him"': kissing the hand is the form of the petition. pese, present subjunctive of pesar, 'to grieve'. desondra, 'dishonour', from ondra, 'honour'.

sentences.t:
El[le] casó mi[es] fijas, ca non gelas di yo;
quando las han dexadas a grant desonor,
si desondra y cabe alguna contra nos,
la poca e la grant toda es de mio señor.
sentences.i: It was he who married my daughters, for I did not give them; now that they have abandoned them in great dishonour, if any dishonour falls on us in this, little or great, it is all my lord's.
sentences.n: El[le] = él, the le Pidal's. casó, 'gave in marriage'. mi[es] = mis, the old mies, the es Pidal's. ca, 'for'. gelas = se las, 'them to them' (ge, the old form of se before lo, la). quando, 'since, now that'. han dexadas, the participle agreeing with las. desonor, 'dishonour' (like desondra; onor of honour, not the house 'estate'). y cabe, 'falls there, falls to one's share' (caber). nos, 'us'. la poca e la grant, 'the little and the great'. The argument is a vassal's: the king made the match (tiradas 102–104), so the shame is the king's — Muño will say it again at v. 2950.

sentences.t:
Mios averes se me an levado, que sobejanos son;
esso me puede pesar con la otra desonor.
sentences.l:
My goods themselves from-me have carried-off, which excessive are;
that me can grieve with the other dishonour.
sentences.i: They have carried off my riches, and those were beyond measure; that can grieve me, along with the other dishonour.
sentences.n: Mios averes, 'my goods, wealth' — what the Çid gave the Infantes on their marriage and their going. se me an levado, 'have been carried off from me': levar = llevar; who carried them is left unsaid. sobejanos, 'excessive, beyond measure'. esso me puede pesar, 'that can grieve me'. con la otra desonor, 'together with the other dishonour'.

sentences.t:
Adúgamelos a vistas, o a juntas o a cortes,
commo aya derecho de ifantes de Carrión,
ca tan grant es la rencura dentro en mi coraçón.”
sentences.l:
May-he-bring-me-them to meeting, or to assemblies or to courts,
so-that I-may-have right of Infantes of Carrión,
for so great is the grievance within in my heart.”
sentences.i: Let him bring them before me at a meeting, or an assembly, or a court, so that I may have justice of the Infantes of Carrión, for great indeed is the grievance within my heart.”
sentences.n: Adúgamelos, present subjunctive of aduzir, 'bring', + me + los, 'let him bring them to me'. Pidal's note to v. 2914: 'vistas o juntas, comp. 2733' — at v. 2733 (Pidal's note there) the vistas, a meeting agreed beforehand, sometimes had a judicial character, like the juntas, the district judicial assemblies, which were always less solemn than the cortes. vistas, 'meeting' (house); juntas, 'assemblies'; cortes, 'courts' (the plural for the occasion), giving ó-e. commo, 'so that'. aver derecho de, 'to have right of, get justice from'. ca, 'for'. rencura, 'grievance' (v. 2862). The speech ends here.

sentences.t:
Muño Gustioz, privado cavalgó,
con él dos cavalleros quel sirvan a so sabor,
e con él escuderos que son de criazón.
sentences.l:
Muño Gustioz, quickly he-rode,
with him two knights that-him may-serve at his pleasure,
and with him squires who are of household-rearing.
sentences.i: Muño Gustioz rode off at once, and with him two knights to serve him at his pleasure, and squires with him who were bred in the household.
sentences.n: privado cavalgó, 'quickly he rode'. quel sirvan = que le sirvan, the present subjunctive of purpose, 'to serve him'. a so sabor, 'at his pleasure', so = su. Pidal's note to v. 2919: 'de criazón, esto es, criados en casa de Cid' — 'that is, brought up in the house of Cid' (de Cid, without the article, as printed): the household folk of v. 2707.

sentences.t:
Salien de Valençia e andan quanto pu[o]den,
nos dan vagar los días e las noches.
sentences.l:
They-went-out from Valençia and they-travel as-much-as they-can,
not-themselves they-give rest the days and the nights.
sentences.i: They rode out of Valencia and travel as fast as they can, giving themselves no rest, days or nights.
sentences.n: Salien = salían, imperfect beside the present andan: epic tense-mixing. quanto pu[o]den, 'as much as they can', pu[o]den = pueden, the o Pidal's, giving ó-e. nos = non se, 'not themselves' (as at vv. 2569, 2617), not the pronoun nos. vagar, 'rest, leisure' (que vagar non se dan, v. 434).

sentences.t: Al rey [don Alfons] en San[t] Fagunt lo falló.
sentences.l: To-the king [don Alfons] in San[t] Fagunt him he-found.
sentences.i: He found King Alfonso at Sahagún.
sentences.n: Al rey … lo falló, the person named with a and taken up by lo: 'the king … he found him'. falló = halló. [don Alfons], both words Pidal's (in italics); San[t], the t Pidal's. San Fagunt is Sahagún, as Pidal's rubric names it. Pidal's note to v. 2922: 'Para la devoción de Alfonso VI al monasterio de Sahagún, v. 1312' — 'For Alfonso VI's devotion to the monastery of Sahagún, see v. 1312'.

sentences.t:
Rey es de Castiella e rey es de León
e de las Asturias bien a San Çalvador,
fasta dentro en Santi Yaguo de todo es señor,
ellos co[m]des gallizanos a él tienen por señor.
sentences.l:
King he-is of Castiella and king he-is of León
and of the Asturias right to San Çalvador,
as-far-as within in Santi Yaguo of all he-is lord,
and-the counts Galician him hold for lord.
sentences.i: He is king of Castile and king of León, and of the Asturias right to Oviedo; as far as Santiago itself he is lord of all, and the counts of Galicia hold him for their lord.
sentences.n: A pause to set out the king's greatness. bien a, 'right up to'. Pidal's note to v. 2924: 'San Çalvador es Oviedo, capital de Asturias, así llamado por tener su catedral consagrada a San Salvador' — 'San Çalvador is Oviedo, capital of Asturias, so called because its cathedral is dedicated to San Salvador (the Holy Saviour)'. fasta dentro en, 'right inside'. Pidal's note to v. 2925: 'Santi Yaguo, la ciudad de Santiago de Galicia' — 'the city of Santiago in Galicia'. ellos is read here as e los, 'and the', the and run onto the article; ellos 'they', in apposition to the counts, is also possible, and the reading is not certain. co[m]des = condes, the m Pidal's. gallizanos, 'Galician'. a él tienen por señor, 'hold him as lord'.

sentences.t:
Assí commo descavalga aquel Muño Gustioz,
omillós a los santos e rogó a[l] Criador;
adeliñó poral palaçio do estava la cort,
con el[le] dos cavalleros quel aguardan cum a sseñor.
sentences.l:
As-soon-as dismounts that Muño Gustioz,
bowed-himself to the saints and prayed to-[the] Creator;
he-made-straight for-the palace where was the court,
with him two knights who-him attend as to lord.
sentences.i: As soon as Muño Gustioz dismounts, he bowed before the saints and prayed to the Creator; then he made straight for the palace where the court was, and with him the two knights who attend him as their lord.
sentences.n: Assí commo, 'as soon as'. descavalga, present among preterites. Pidal's note to v. 2928: 'omillós, "saludó reverentemente", v. 1396, y para la oración en el lugar de llegada, v. 1394' — 'he greeted reverently, v. 1396; and for the prayer on arriving, v. 1394': omillós = se omilló, he bowed in the church before the saints' altars. a[l], the l Pidal's. adeliñó poral, 'made straight for the' (poral = pora el). do = donde. el[le] = él, the le Pidal's. quel aguardan = que le aguardan, 'who attend him'. cum = como; sseñor, ss as printed. Pidal's margin prints 2030 against this line, a misprint for 2930.

sentences.i: As soon as they came into the midst of the court, the king saw them and knew Muño Gustioz; the king rose, and received them very well.
sentences.n: por medio de la cort, 'through the midst of the court'. ví[d]olos = viólos, 'he saw them', from the old preterite vido, the d Pidal's. coñosció, 'recognized'. levantós = se levantó, 'rose' — a high mark of favour. tan bien los reçibió, 'so well he received them', set beside it without a link.

sentences.t:
Delant el rey [Alfons] los inojos fincó,
besábale los pie[de]s aquel Muño Gustioz;
sentences.l:
Before the king [Alfons] the knees he-planted,
was-kissing-him the feet that Muño Gustioz;
sentences.i: Before King Alfonso he went down on his knees, and Muño Gustioz kissed the king's feet:
sentences.n: Delant el rey, 'before the king'. [Alfons], Pidal's (in italics). los inojos fincó, 'he planted his knees', knelt (inojos = hinojos, fincar 'to fix, plant'). besábale = le besaba, imperfect. pie[de]s = pies, the old piedes, the de Pidal's.

sentences.i: “Mercy, O king, whom men call lord of many kingdoms! The Campeador kisses your feet and your hands; he is your vassal, and you are his lord.
sentences.n: Merçed, 'mercy, grace', the word that opens a petition. Pidal's note to v. 2936: 'largos reynos, "muchos reinos"; comp. 804' — 'many kingdoms'. a vos dizen señor, 'whom they call lord'. elle = él. so señor, 'his lord'. Muño uses vos to the king throughout.

sentences.t:
Casastes sus fijas con ifantes de Carrión,
alto f[o] el casamien[t]o ca lo quisiestes vos!
sentences.l:
You-married his daughters with Infantes of Carrión,
high was the marriage for it willed you!
sentences.i: You married his daughters to the Infantes of Carrión — a lofty match, since it was you who willed it!
sentences.n: Casastes = casasteis, 'you married (them off)', casar con, 'to marry to'. f[o] = fue, the o Pidal's; casamien[t]o, the t Pidal's. alto, 'high, lofty'. ca lo quisiestes vos, 'for you wished it', vos stressed at the end: the honour of the match was the king's doing.

sentences.i: You know well what honour that marriage brought us, and how the Infantes of Carrión have now disgraced us: they cruelly beat the daughters of the Çid Campeador;
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 2941: '"Ya sabéis cuánta honra nos ha proporcionado ese casamiento con familia tan noble". Muño Gustioz se tiene él mismo por deshonrado, como todos los de la casa del Cid, v. p. 93, n. 1' — '"You know how much honour that marriage into so noble a family has brought us." Muño Gustioz holds himself dishonoured, like all those of the Cid's house; see p. 93, n. 1' (his introduction). es cuntida, 'has befallen', ser as auxiliary; cuntir, as at v. 2852. qu[o]mo = como, the o Pidal's. infantes, spelled with n here, as printed. abiltados, 'debased, disgraced' (abiltar, v. 2732), agreeing with nos. mal majaron, 'cruelly beat' (majar, 'to pound'). sus fijas del Çid, 'his daughters of the Çid', the possessive and the de together.

sentences.t:
majadas e desnudas a grande desonor,
desenparadas las dexaron en el robredo de Corpes,
a las bestias fieras e a las aves del mont.
sentences.l:
beaten and stripped to great dishonour,
forsaken them they-left in the oak-wood of Corpes,
to the beasts wild and to the birds of-the wood.
sentences.i: beaten and stripped, to their great dishonour, they left them forsaken in the oak-wood of Corpes, to the wild beasts and the birds of the woods.
sentences.n: majadas e desnudas, 'beaten and stripped'. a grande desonor, 'to great dishonour'. desenparadas, 'forsaken, left without protection' (desamparar). robredo, 'oak-wood'; Corpes, giving ó-e. mont = monte, 'wood' (house: montes 'woods').

sentences.t: Afélas sus fijas en Valençia do son.
sentences.l: Behold-them his daughters in Valençia where they-are.
sentences.i: There they are now, his daughters, in Valencia.
sentences.n: Afélas = afé + las, 'behold them' (as félos, v. 2647; afevos, v. 1499): the daughters are in Valencia, where they are, safe at home. do = donde.

sentences.i: For this he kisses your hands, as vassal to lord, that you may bring them before him at a meeting, or an assembly, or a court; he holds himself dishonoured, but your dishonour is the greater,
sentences.n: Por esto, 'for this'. que gelos levedes, 'that you bring them to him': gelos = se los (to him, them), levedes, present subjunctive of levar; the Çid's own words of v. 2914 again. tienes = tiénese, 'he holds himself'. Pidal's note to v. 2950: '"se tiene por deshonrado, mas vuestra [deshonra] es mayor"; comp. 511 para el sustantivo embebido en el verbo' — '"he holds himself dishonoured, but your [dishonour] is greater"; compare 511 for the noun contained within the verb': la vuestra, 'yours', stands for a deshonra that is only implied in desondrado.

sentences.t:
e que vos pese, rey, commo sodes sabidor;
que aya mio Çid derecho de ifantes de Carrión.”
sentences.l:
and that to-you it-may-grieve, king, as you-are wise;
that may-have my Çid right of Infantes of Carrión.”
sentences.i: and he begs that it may grieve you, O king, as the wise man you are, and that my Çid may have justice of the Infantes of Carrión.”
sentences.n: e que vos pese, 'and that it may grieve you', still hanging on vos besa las manos, the form of petition (as v. 2907). sabidor, 'knowing, wise'. que aya … derecho de, 'that he may have justice of', aver derecho as at v. 2915. The speech ends here.

sentences.t: El rey una grand ora calló e comidió;
sentences.l: The king a great hour was-silent and pondered;
sentences.i: For a long while the king was silent and pondered.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 2953: '"un gran rato", v. 1889' — 'a good while': una grand ora, 'for a long while' (house). comidió, 'pondered, reflected' (comedir). Pidal ends the line with a semicolon before the speech.

sentences.i: “I tell you truly, it grieves me to the heart; and you speak the truth in this, Muño Gustioz, for it was I who married his daughters to the Infantes of Carrión;
sentences.n: The king speaks tú to the messenger (te digo, dizes, tú), where Muño spoke vos to the king. me pesa de coraçón, 'it grieves me from the heart'. ca, 'for'. casé … con, 'married to'.

sentences.t:
fizlo por bien, que ff[o]sse a su pro.
¡Si quier el casamiento fecho non f[o]sse oy!
Entre yo e mio Çid pésanos de coraçón.
sentences.l:
I-did-it for good, that it-should-be to his advantage.
If-only the marriage made not were today!
Between I and my Çid it-grieves-us from heart.
sentences.i: I did it for the best, that it might be to his advantage. Would that the marriage had never been made! It grieves us both to the heart, myself and my Çid.
sentences.n: fizlo = lo hice, from fiz, the short preterite of fazer. ff[o]sse = fuese, the o Pidal's, ff as printed. pro, 'profit, advantage'. Pidal's note to v. 2958: 'Si quier!, "ojalá"' — 'would that!'; f[o]sse = fuese, the o Pidal's; oy = hoy. Pidal's note to v. 2959: '"Tanto a mí como a mio Cid"' — '"Me as much as my Cid"': Entre yo e mio Çid, 'between me and my Çid', both of us; pésanos, 'it grieves us'.

sentences.t: Ayudar lê a derecho, sín salve el Criador!
sentences.l: To-help him I-will to right, so-me may-save the Creator!
sentences.i: I will help him to his right, so may the Creator save me!
sentences.n: Ayudar lê, the split future: lê = le + e (he, 'I will', written without h), run together and marked by Pidal's circumflex, as lâ, lês, mê: ayudar le he = le ayudaré, 'I will help him'. a derecho, 'to his right, in justice'. sín, most likely sí + me ('so me'), the m written n: 'so may the Creator save me', an oath like sí vos vala el Criador; the reading of sín is not certain, and Pidal gives no note.

sentences.t:
Lo que non cuydava fer de toda esta sazón,
andarán mios porteros por todo [el] reyno mio,
pora dentro en Toledo pregonarán mi[e] cort,
que allá me vayan cue[m]des e ifançones;
sentences.i: Though I had no thought of it at all this season, my officers shall go through all my kingdom and proclaim my court to be held at Toledo, so that counts and nobles may come to me there;
sentences.n: Lo que non cuydava fer, 'what I was not thinking to do' (cuydar, 'to think, intend'; fer, short for fazer): a court at this time had not been in his mind. de toda esta sazón, 'in all this season'. [el], Pidal's; reyno mio, the possessive after the noun (an ó-line on mio; Pidal gives no note on the rhyme). porteros, 'officers', the king's summoners. Pidal's note to v. 2963: 'El rey escoge la cort como medio de enjuiciamiento y reparación más solemne que las vistas o juntas.—El portero (v. 1380) es, naturalmente, el encargado de convocar la corte pregonada (3272) o solemne' — 'The king chooses the court as a means of judgement and redress more solemn than the vistas or juntas.—The portero (v. 1380) is, naturally, the one charged with summoning the proclaimed court (3272), the solemn one.' pora dentro en Toledo, 'for within Toledo'. pregonarán, 'they will proclaim'. mi[e] = mi, the old mie, the e Pidal's. cue[m]des = condes, the m Pidal's. ifançones, 'lesser nobles', below the counts (as at v. 2072).

sentences.t:
mandaré commo i vayan ifantes de Carrión,
e commo den derecho a mio Çid el Campeador,
e que non aya rencura podiéndolo veda[r] yo.
sentences.l:
I-will-order that there may-go Infantes of Carrión,
and that they-may-give right to my Çid the Campeador,
and that not he-may-have grievance being-able-it to-prevent I.
sentences.i: and I will command that the Infantes of Carrión go there, and that they do right by my Çid the Campeador, and that he shall have no grievance, so far as I can prevent it.
sentences.n: mandaré commo, 'I will order that' (commo = que after a verb of ordering). i = allí, 'there'. den derecho a, 'give right to, do justice to'. rencura, 'grievance'. podiéndolo veda[r] yo, 'I being able to prevent it', i.e. as far as I can; vedar, 'to forbid, prevent', the r Pidal's. No closing quote: the king's speech runs on into tirada 134 (Pidal: El rey convoca corte en Toledo), with a new assonance, and the next part.
